definition.model_summary: Ask which real activities the runtime is running right now.
definition.model_description: Answers a question about what real executors are running, from the runtime's own in-memory activity facts. Use by=resource with a verified target to find another writer of a file you just operated on - including one in another session or workspace that really touches the same physical object. Use by=unknown_write_set to find a Shell whose write set cannot be proven. Use by=group or by=session to list your own running tools, and by=exact to look one up by the id a previous answer gave you. It is read-only: it takes no file protection, starts and stops nothing, cannot change any tool's outcome, and cannot widen what your session may see. A matching target query echoes your own known spelling; it does not disclose another session's private paths or parameters. The result always reports its coverage, so zero rows with complete coverage (nothing is running) is never the same answer as an index that could not be read.

document.description:
S04.5 B/R4: the **model-facing** input of the run-information query.

WHY IT LIVES HERE AND NOT IN THE TOOL CONTRACT
The query's own contract already lives in this crate (`ActivityQueryRequestV1`), and this is the
same question asked by a different caller. Putting it in `aura-tool-contract` would make that
low-level crate depend on this one and invert the dependency direction the design fixes; here it
sits beside the wire shape it mirrors, so the two cannot drift.

WHY IT IS THIS SMALL, AND WHAT IT DELIBERATELY CANNOT SAY
The model may name **what it is looking for** and nothing else. It cannot name a session, a
workspace or a grant: those are resolved from the step's own authenticated position exactly as
the IPC route resolves them. A model that could name its own session would widen its own
visibility by asking, which is the defect R4 names. `target` is a **lookup hint, not a grant** -
it names an already-verified object the caller is asking about, and it can only ever match a fact
a real publisher recorded.

ActivityExecutionRef.description:
The real execution reference an activity is derived from.

Every variant names identities the publishing owner really holds. The Agent
variants carry the real `ToolCall`/`Operation`/`Attempt`; the non-Agent
variants carry the identity that owner actually has, so no Agent identity is
fabricated for Main, a buffer commit or a managed background process.

oneOf.description: The Agent's own tool call, bound to its real operation and attempt.

A file command owned by Main's filesystem service.

R1: the operation identity is the real one the broker minted for this dispatch, and the
command invocation is carried only when the request genuinely has one. An earlier version
byte-converted a `CommandInvocationId` into a `MutationJournalId` and presented it as a
journal identity Main never owned; that field is gone rather than re-typed, because a
fabricated identity is worse than an absent one.
A buffer commit identified by its own editor reservation and revision.
A P04 workspace publication identified by Main's lifecycle operation.
A real P04 file publication; a correlation is not a lifecycle or deferred-mutation ID.
A managed Shell execution identified by its real reserved attempt.
A Shell invocation owned by the Agent's command execution service.

The set is closed on purpose. A new publisher is a real new owner of a real
side effect, and it has to be named here before it can publish.

A Shell command the Agent runs in the foreground of its own call.
A Shell process the managed background owner still holds.

ActivityResourceRelation.description:
What kind of access the executor has against one real target.

`UnknownWriteSet` is not a placeholder for "we did not look": it is the honest
answer for a Shell whose write set cannot be proven, within its own workspace.
`UnknownWriteSetOutsideWorkspace` is that answer for a Shell whose script names places
outside its workspace. Neither serialises globally or disables Shell.

document.description:
R4: the result of the model-executable run-information query.

It is the wire response's page type, holding only the calling session's own rows; rows of other
sessions are counted as filtered. Nothing here is a permission decision - the page carries only
rows the caller was already allowed to see.

definition.model_summary: Describe an exact tool version from an exact registry snapshot.
definition.model_description: Returns the complete model-visible contract for one exact ToolId and ToolVersion from the supplied immutable Tool Registry Snapshot. It never substitutes a newer version. The result describes the frozen schema, result contract, source, audience, capabilities, resource requirements, and current loadability.

definition.model_summary: List the exact tools exposed in the supplied registry snapshot.
definition.model_description: Lists the Core, pinned, and TurnTask-ephemeral tools exposed by one exact immutable Tool Registry Snapshot. It does not search the global registry, modify exposure, or substitute a newer snapshot.

definition.model_summary: Atomically load exact tool versions for later model steps in this TurnTask.
definition.model_description: Atomically exposes one or more exact tool versions as TurnTask-scoped ephemeral tools. All targets are validated before any change is committed. The operation does not install, trust, enable, or pin tools. Successfully loaded tools become available only in a newly created registry snapshot for a later model step.

definition.model_summary: Search discoverable tools in the caller's exact registry snapshot.
definition.model_description: Searches the immutable Tool Registry Snapshot available to the current agent by canonical name, display name, summary, and model description. Returns exact ToolId and ToolVersion references and an opaque cursor. It does not install, trust, pin, load, unload, or execute a tool. Use tools.describe to inspect an exact result and tools.load to expose selected tools to a later model step.

definition.model_summary: Atomically unload TurnTask-scoped ephemeral tools for later model steps.
definition.model_description: Atomically removes one or more exact TurnTask-scoped ephemeral tool exposures. It cannot remove Core tools, Workspace pins, or Session pins. A target that is already not ephemerally loaded is an idempotent no-op. Any real change creates a new immutable registry snapshot.
